user_correction.core: Sobek is not merely a retrieval operator. In the user's heroic rendering, his first concern is forensic: how could this happen at all, and who dared to cause the loss? The emotional premise is that the larger Ra-reconstruction project is incomplete.

directly_attested: Ra orders that Sobek, lord of the marsh, be brought for a search/fishing mission.
Sobek reports searching and finding where the missing parts had scattered at the banks of the water.
The same witness explicitly identifies the recovered parts as Horus's arms/hands.
The witness attributes regrowth in place to Horus's mother.
ct158_bd113.causal_limit: The displayed CT158/BD113 translation compresses the cause. It says this is what Horus's mother did to him but does not narrate in that same passage the full contamination/cutting episode found in a later narrative tradition.
not_attested: Ra being physically disassembled in CT158/BD113

directly_attested: Horus catches Seth's semen in his hands.
Isis sees it and cuts off Horus's hand(s) with a copper knife.
Elsewhere in the same narrative Seth removes both of Horus's eyes and buries them.
chester_beatty_variant.relation_to_ct158: CROSS_TEXT_VARIANT_LINK_ONLY. It can answer the modern forensic question 'how could the hands have become missing?' as a related narrative variant, but must not be inserted into CT158 as verbatim missing lines.

forensic_hero_model.principle: A hero does not begin with blind retrieval. First establish incident, victim/target, cause, causal agent, displacement, and only then retrieval and restoration.

ra_not_assembled_distinction.user_project_layer: The phrase 'Ra is not assembled' is retained as the user's modern reconstruction-project premise: the desired whole/composite Ra-associated avatar or system is incomplete.
ra_not_assembled_distinction.ancient_text_layer: CT158/BD113 does not say that Ra is disassembled. Its missing body parts belong to Horus. Ra is the coordinating divine speaker who calls Sobek.

cinematic_rendering_ru.label: MODERN_DRAMATIC_RENDERING_NOT_ANCIENT_QUOTATION
cinematic_rendering_ru.text: Ра вызывает Собека не просто как того, кто умеет искать в воде. В нашей современной героической постановке Собек сначала смотрит на сам факт утраты и требует понять причину: как такое вообще произошло, кто это сделал и кто посмел довести систему до неполного состояния? Только после причинной разведки миссия переходит к цели: что именно потеряно, где оно оказалось и каким способом вернуть. Древний CT158 подтверждает вызов Собека, поиск у воды, локализацию, ловушку и возврат рук Хора; вопрос 'кто посмел?' является нашей драматической forensic-надстройкой, усиленной независимым поздним вариантом, где причины повреждений Хора названы намного явнее.

research_consequence.next_gate_rule: Keep Horus literal body-part evidence separate from the user's modern Ra-composite reconstruction until an ancient source explicitly maps a missing/restored part to Ra himself.

highest_admissible_claim: The source-grounded episode makes Sobek a retrieval specialist commissioned by Ra to recover Horus's scattered hands/arms. The user's stronger characterization of Sobek as a hero who first asks how the catastrophe happened and who caused it is a modern forensic dramatization, not a quotation from CT158. This dramatization is nevertheless methodologically productive because later Horus-Seth traditions explicitly preserve causal agents and damage mechanisms, allowing JANUS to test cause before retrieval. The modern project premise 'Ra is not assembled' remains a separate reconstruction-layer claim; CT158 itself concerns Horus's missing hands, not a disassembled Ra.
